Meh. Nothing particularly special about any of these. After several hours in the game you'll have seen stuff mostly like this several times.

There really isn't any reason to visit anything but blue and green stars once you have the warp upgrades.. Just go to free explore mode after moving down the path to the center of the galaxy up to the last star and find the nearest blue or green star at the end and warp to it instead.

Green and Blue stars also tend to have more hazard planets FYI. So it's worth investing in hazard shielding if you're traveling through them if you've got enough slots for them.

I recommend hanging around your starting system until you get the Warp Drives fully upgraded. It doesn't really take that long to do it, and most of the time you'll find everything you need to build them in your starter system if you root around enough.

The ending sucks though. There isn't one. It just drops you in a new galaxy. That's not a spoiler because there's nothing to spoil. Doesn't even run credits or anything, you just zoom out in the map and you're in a new galaxy. All your systems are broken and need repairs, but you still have your ship and all the upgrades you've gathered.

Also, the difficulty of the second galaxy is slightly harder. More hostile critters, drones are a bit faster about turning aggro, and you'll run into hazard planets more often.

Game is not worth $60. It's a great indie title, but people expecting more than that will be disappointed. This should have been $29 tops at full price.
